overall_visual_style: Stylised anime-inspired illustration with expressive eyes, clean line art, cel shading, dynamic compositions, and polished modern character design. Palette: sky blue, peach, cream, navy, leaf green. Lighting: clean cinematic light, cel-shaded shadows, bright highlights. Mood: youthful, emotive, cinematic, polished. Avoid: photorealism, any text, letters, numbers or logos, the name or look of a real artist, hyper-detailed skin texture, messy painterly strokes.

shots.shot_goal: Name the viewer's own quiet plateau in a single recognisable image: a fine job, a fine routine, and no movement in it.
shots.frame_composition: Interior of a calm, tidy office in early morning. Medium shot from slightly behind and to one side of the reel's recurring character, who sits motionless at a plain cream desk, shoulders lowered, chin propped on one hand, gaze aimed past the desk at nothing in particular. The desk is bare except for a cold mug and a small leaf-green potted plant; no screens, papers, boards or signage anywhere in the room. A tall window on the left throws clean cinematic sky-blue daylight across cream walls, cel-shaded shadow pooling under the desk and along the navy chair back. The upper third of the frame is open empty wall.
shots.motion_plan: Very slow push in on the seated figure, closing gently from medium to medium-close over the whole shot, so the room quietly tightens around a person who is not moving.
shots.source_support: The cited card describes being plateaued in a job and routine that are fine, with every small change looking worse, so the person stays put exactly where they are. The picture shows only that: an ordinary workplace and a person holding still, adding no event or outcome the card does not state.
shots.video_motion_intent: The seated figure breathes out and their shoulders slump slightly lower, then settle and hold still.

shots.shot_goal: Hand the idea to one concrete creature and make the direction of travel physical: the exit begins by going deeper in.
shots.frame_composition: Underwater, inside a slatted wooden lobster trap resting on pale sand. Medium-close, fully side-on framing: a single peach-shelled lobster low in the frame, body angled toward the shadowed centre of the cage on the left, legs mid-stride, antennae trailing behind it. To the right, the funnel entrance glows with bright sky-blue open water; the cage interior the lobster faces is deep navy, banded by hard cel-shaded slat shadows falling across the sand. Clean cinematic underwater light, crisp line art on the shell, bright highlights along its back. No lettering, markings or buoys anywhere in frame.
shots.motion_plan: Slow lateral drift of the frame from right to left, travelling with the lobster away from the bright opening and into the banded shadow at the cage's centre.
shots.source_support: The cited card states the lobster must move deeper into the cage first, back toward the centre, before it can ever reach the opening. The frame stages exactly that geometry — bright opening behind, dark centre ahead — and shows no escape, which the card does not grant.
shots.video_motion_intent: The lobster walks steadily sideways across the frame into the darker part of the cage, legs stepping in rhythm, antennae trailing.

shots.shot_goal: Land the reversal: the instinct toward the light is sensible, and it is exactly what keeps the creature caught.
shots.frame_composition: Close side-on shot inside the same slatted wooden trap. The peach-shelled lobster is pressed up against the bright wall of the cage, claws raised against the slats, its whole body leaning toward the glow. Behind and around it the cage interior falls away into navy shadow. Sky-blue light blooms hard through the gaps between the slats, cutting bright cel-shaded bars across the shell and the sand below and throwing long stripes into the dark behind. Fine silt hangs in the beams. Clean cinematic underwater light, bright rim highlights on the raised claws. No lettering or markings anywhere.
shots.motion_plan: Slow push in past the lobster's raised claws toward the blooming light between the slats, so the glow steadily fills more of the frame while the creature stays exactly where it is.
shots.text_overlay: the one direction that feels wrong
shots.source_support: The cited card states every instinct pulls the lobster away from the tight space and toward the light, so it stays trapped by its own good sense. The picture shows the creature still pressed to the lit wall and still inside the trap, asserting no escape.
shots.video_motion_intent: Light through the slats ripples and shifts gently across the lobster's shell and the sand, as the water above slowly moves.

shots.shot_goal: Turn the metaphor toward the viewer: a small rise in fog that feels, from inside it, like the summit.
shots.frame_composition: Wide exterior shot of a low grassy rise swallowed in thick pale fog. The reel's recurring character stands near the crest, small in the frame and seen from behind, facing out into blank white. Leaf-green grass and a few bent stems show at their feet, and the ground falls gently away on every visible side before dissolving into cream-white fog within a few metres. Cool sky-blue daylight comes diffuse from above with soft cel-shaded shadow under the grass tufts; a faint peach warmth glows somewhere high in the murk. Nothing else is visible — no path, marker, structure or signage.
shots.motion_plan: Begin slightly tight on the figure and ease outward to a wider frame, letting the featureless fog grow around them until the small rise reads as the only ground there is.
shots.source_support: The cited card describes standing on a hill in thick fog where the ground falls away in every direction so it feels like the very top. The frame illustrates that described situation and nothing more.
shots.video_motion_intent: Thick fog drifts slowly and continuously sideways across the slope, thinning and thickening as it passes the standing figure.

shots.shot_goal: Open the trapped feeling into possibility: something far higher exists across the valley, reachable only by going down first.
shots.frame_composition: Wide exterior shot from just behind and to one side of the same rise. The recurring character stands in profile at the crest's edge, one foot already set on the ground sloping downward, body turned toward a deep fog-filled valley. Across that valley the thinning cloud shows the faint navy silhouette of a far larger mountain, its upper flank catching clean peach light, its base still buried in cream-white fog. Leaf-green grass at the crest, sky-blue sky brightening above the cloud layer, crisp cel-shaded shadow along the slope. No path, markers or structures anywhere.
shots.motion_plan: Gentle lateral drift across the valley from the figure at the crest toward the distant peak, with a barely perceptible lift, so the far summit slides into view as the frame travels.
shots.source_support: The cited card states a far higher peak could be sitting just across the valley, hidden in the clouds, and that you would never find it while you refuse to walk downhill. The peak is drawn faint and half-hidden and the figure has only begun to step down — the card promises no arrival.
shots.video_motion_intent: Fog drifts steadily across the valley, thinning and gathering so the distant peak's silhouette firms and softens again.

shots.shot_goal: Settle the payoff and leave the question with the viewer: the descent already begun, the cost accepted.
shots.frame_composition: Medium-wide exterior seen from slightly below, on the descending hillside. The recurring character stands a few steps down from the crest, fog now at waist height around them, body half-turned toward the valley and head lifted toward the far ridge. The crest they left sits small and pale behind and above them. Warm peach light spreads along the distant ridgeline and catches the top of the fog; cool sky-blue shadow fills the slope below. Leaf-green grass breaks through the fog near the figure's feet. Generous empty fog in the lower third of the frame. No path, structures, markers or signage.
shots.motion_plan: Slow, steady push in on the figure standing below the crest, easing to a near stop on the held frame so the shot settles rather than arrives.
shots.text_overlay: What's the step back you keep refusing?
shots.source_support: The cited card's closing line is that a worse move today can be exactly the price of a better peak tomorrow, reached by accepting a step backward on purpose. The picture shows a figure who has taken a lower position on the slope with the far ridge lit ahead — the card's own payoff, with no author, book or named term depicted, since that card's uncertainties leave their identity unestablished.
